Solo Road Trip · Oct 7 to 12, 2026

San Francisco → Mount Shasta

McCloud Falls, all three

Lower, Middle and Upper Falls are linked by an easy trail along the McCloud River. The Forest Service puts the full round trip at roughly 3 miles, and other guides say up to 3.8 depending on where you park. Plan 2 to 2.5 hours. Parking is free at each of the three lots. Short on time? Lower and Middle are the best two.

Eat in Mount Shasta town, then check in at Lake Siskiyou Camp Resort. Sunset is around 6:30pm in early October and earlier as the month goes on. Watch Mount Shasta from the lake shore.

Garfield Peak Trail

Starts at Rim Village and climbs above the caldera the whole way, with wide views of the lake and Wizard Island. It is about 3.4 miles round trip with roughly 1,000 to 1,250 feet of climbing depending on the source. Plan 2 to 2.5 hours. Park entry is $30 per vehicle, good for 7 days (May 22 to Oct 31).

Watchman Peak

The short one, and the best view of Wizard Island. About 1.6 miles round trip, roughly 45 to 60 minutes. Skip it if you are behind. You want to be through the North Entrance by about 4:15pm.

Optional, only if out of the park by 3:30pmWaterfall0.8 mi RT

Toketee Falls

About 0.8 miles round trip with roughly 127 feet of climbing, to a 90-foot two-tier waterfall over columnar basalt. Your old plan listed 0.4 miles, which was the one-way distance. Skip it if it is getting dark. Watson Falls (0.6 to 1.6 mi) is a bit closer if you want a shorter one.

Whistler's Bend County Park, near Roseburg

Sits on the North Umpqua, right along Hwy 138. Dry sites are about $40, and the park has flush toilets. Dinner in Glide or Roseburg on the way in (not researched, pick on the day). Sunrise on the river tomorrow.

11:15amHike7.2 mi loop$10 to $12

Trail of Ten Falls, Silver Falls State Park

Ten waterfalls in one loop, including South Falls at 177 ft and Double Falls at 178 ft, with trails that walk behind several of them. Oregon State Parks lists it at 7.2 miles; one guide says 7.8, with about 800 to 1,300 feet of climbing depending on the source. Plan 3 to 5 hours. Day use is $10 for Oregon plates and about $12 for out of state, paid at the kiosk. Dogs are not allowed on the canyon trails. Eat at the South Falls Lodge if it is open, or carry snacks.

Ainsworth to Northwest Portland

About 32 miles to the Lower Macleay trailhead. Saturday is the busiest day for Portland's trails, so an early start matters. You begin with a mostly full battery from last night's Portland charge.

9:00amHike5.7 mi RT~950 ft gain

Lower Macleay to Pittock Mansion

Follow Balch Creek up through old-growth Douglas fir (including Portland's tallest tree at 243 ft), then climb the Wildwood Trail to the mansion. About 5.7 miles round trip, roughly 3 hours with time at the top. If you want it shorter, the Tunnel Trailhead on Cornell Rd gets you there in about 3.7 miles round trip.

Pittock Mansion

Open 10am to 5pm through October, and the grounds and the skyline view are free. The house tour is $16.50 if you want it. On a clear day you can see Mount Hood and Mount St. Helens.

Ainsworth to Angels Rest

About 15 miles west on I-84 to the Bridal Veil exit. Oregon Hikers advises arriving before 8:30am on weekends because the lots fill up, and today is a Sunday.

7:35amHike4.8 mi RT~1,475 ft gain$12 out of state

Angels Rest

A steady climb to a rocky point with a 270 degree view of the Columbia River. About 4.8 miles round trip, roughly 2.5 to 3 hours. Oregon State Parks charges $10 for Oregon plates and $12 out of state. The east wind can be fierce in fall, so bring a layer and keep your hat on. Most of the trail burned in the 2017 Eagle Creek Fire and is regrowing, so there is less shade than it used to have.

Map it →Trail guide →

~20 min · I-84 east, back past Ainsworth
10:50amWaterfallNo permit needed

Multnomah Falls, quick visit

Oregon's tallest waterfall. The timed-use permit only ran May 22 to Sep 7, 2026, so you can walk right up. Expect crowds on a Sunday. The paved path to Benson Bridge is short and steep. Give it 40 minutes, and skip it if you are running late.

Reserve These

Book Ahead

Four campsites need a reservation, and Ainsworth is the most urgent because Friday and Saturday nights fill first. Everything else is pay at the gate or free. Prices and rules are as of late September 2026, so confirm at booking.

⛺
Reserve

Night 1: Lake Siskiyou Camp Resort

Book online or call 530-926-2618. I could not find current tent site rates, so the price is unconfirmed. Ask when you book whether car camping in a tent site is allowed.

Book →

⛺
Reserve

Night 2: Whistler's Bend County Park

About $40 for a dry site, plus a $10 online fee. Book up to 11 months ahead online at douglascountyor.gov or by calling 541-957-7001. Open year-round.

⛺
Reserve

Nights 3 and 4: Ainsworth State Park

Book both nights on ReserveAmerica (Oregon State Parks), which opens 6 months ahead. To sleep in the car you need a drive-in site, and those are the 40 full-hookup sites, about $29 for Oregon residents and $36 for others, plus an $8 booking fee. The 6 tent sites are walk-in only. The campground closes Oct 31. If you own a 14-50 adapter, ask the park whether EV charging at your site is allowed. I could not confirm that policy.

Book →

⛺
Reserve

Night 5: Valley of the Rogue State Park

Book on ReserveAmerica (Oregon State Parks). To sleep in the car you need a drive-in site, meaning one of the standard sites, not the tent-only loop. I could not confirm the standard site price, and tent sites run about $19 to $26. There is an $8 booking fee. Emigrant Lake near Ashland was dropped: its online booking closes 15 days out, Oak Slope closes mid-October.

Book →

Before You Go

Good to Know

Charging, conditions, and backup plans for a solo, non-long-range Tesla trip.

⚡

Range reality check

Rated range is not highway range. Plan for about 200 miles per full charge at 70 mph, less in the cold, on grades, or with Camp Mode running. Every leg in this plan is 150 miles or under, except Day 2's run from Klamath Falls to camp (about 190 miles, but mostly downhill).

🔋

Charger list

  • Williams: 464 6th St
  • Redding: 1900 Hilltop Dr
  • Mount Shasta: 134 Morgan Way
  • Klamath Falls: 2655 Shasta Way
  • Sutherlin: 116 Clover Leaf Loop
  • Grants Pass: 1900 NW 6th St
  • Salem: 3790 Center St NE
  • Portland: 805 SW Broadway
  • Medford: 2000 Crater Lake Hwy

Stall counts came from Tesla and owner-forum listings and can change. Confirm in the car's navigation.

🌌

Crater Lake conditions

  • Rim Drive is typically open until snow closes it, sometimes as early as mid-October. Check NPS road status the morning of Day 2.
  • The North Entrance road closes for the season Nov 1.
  • Cleetwood Cove Trail and the boat dock are closed through 2028, so there is no lake access.
  • East Rim Drive has 2026 construction limits.
↻

Plan B if the North Entrance is closed

Leave the park by OR-62 west to Medford (about 85 miles, downhill), charge at the Medford Supercharger, then take I-5 north to Roseburg. You lose Toketee and add about an hour, but you keep the day.

🌡

Daylight and weather

Sunset runs from about 6:25pm on Oct 7 to about 6:10pm on Oct 12 (approximate). Rain usually settles in by mid to late October, and the Cascades can see early snow. Carry a headlamp, layers, and chains if you are crossing the mountains after mid-October.

⚠

Road and fire alerts

Check TripCheck (dial 511 in Oregon) for road closures, Caltrans QuickMap for California, and InciWeb for wildfires. Smoke can close trailheads and park roads with little notice in early fall.

🧭

Trail safety, solo

  • Cell coverage is patchy at Crater Lake, along Hwy 138, and in the Gorge. Download offline maps for each day.
  • Tell someone your route and your camp each night.
  • Angels Rest: fierce east wind in fall, steep drop-offs at the top, and little shade after the 2017 fire.
  • Silver Falls: trails behind the falls can be slick. No dogs on the canyon trails.
  • Carry water, snacks and a headlamp on every hike.
📞

Emergency

Dial 911 anywhere. If you have no signal, drive to the nearest town or ranger station. Sleep only in the booked campgrounds. Do not overnight at trailheads or rest stops.

❓
